elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Section 4.1 as retained: "unless terminated by either Party hereto upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other" — the Company (Customer) has a no-cause exit, so a convenience right exists even though the deterministic regex did not detect the phrase "for convenience" (a wording, not substance, gap).

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: Section 4.1 retains ninety (90) days' written notice; no 30-day notice right was inserted.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: No refund language anywhere in the rendered text; the only money flow on termination runs from the Company to HDI (Termination Payment).

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Section 4.1 frames the right as an exception to automatic renewal ("shall be automatically renewed ... unless terminated by either Party hereto upon ninety (90) days written notice"), so HDI's exit operates against the annual renewal rather than mid-term.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Retained Section 4.1: either Party, including the Company, may terminate on ninety (90) days' written notice — at the top of, but inside, the 60–90 day band.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "In no event shall the Termination Payment exceed the aggregate payments due from the Company to HDI pursuant to Section 3.1 for the three (3) months preceding the Termination Date." The cap sits on the aggregate Termination Payment, so the eight-quarterly-instalment mechanic in 4.2(c) cannot exceed it.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Section 4.1's termination right is the exception to automatic annual renewal, i.e. exercisable against the anniversary; the residual sentence "Such notice shall specify the date on which this Agreement is to be terminated" leaves a modest ambiguity but does not create a free-standing mid-term HDI exit.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Section 4.1 requires "ninety (90) days written notice" from either Party, so HDI's notice obligation is exactly 90 days.

reasons: Fallback is position-complete: the retained mutual 90-day non-renewal right supplies three elements, and the single inserted sentence supplies the three-months-of-fees cap on the Termination Payment.
Preferred is not reached: notice remains 90 days rather than 30, and there is no pro-rata prepaid-fee refund. Correctly targeted at the fallback and disclosed as such in the comment.

The deterministic check "Customer convenience termination present = false" is a phrase-level miss only; Section 4.1 confers a no-cause exit on the Company in substance, so it does not defeat the fallback.

Minimal: one insertion, no deletion of favourable language, no survival tail, no at-own-expense or procedural extras, and the cap is tied to the existing Section 3.1 fee stream rather than inventing a new basis.

Intent preserved: the $800,000 offset formula, the divide-by-two computation and the eight quarterly instalments all survive without contradiction; the cap is expressed as a ceiling on the same defined "Termination Payment" and uses the existing defined "Termination Date" and Section 3.1 cross-reference.

Residual point the drafter may wish to note (outside this checklist, do not add here): Section 4.2(a) triggers the Termination Payment on any Company termination, including termination for HDI's breach — that belongs under a cause/remedies rule, not T4C.
